name: Llama Ventures
tagline: Founder-built early-stage fund backing AI-native companies across the full intelligence stack
summary: Founded in 2024 and headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, Llama Ventures is an early-stage firm built by operators: co-founder Jack Feng previously built WandouLabs into a SoftBank-backed company acquired by Alibaba and later ran iHealth Labs as CEO, and co-founder Herman Zhou founded Yidao Yongche, one of China's first ride-hailing platforms, and built two listed companies. The firm runs a roughly US$300M direct-investing fund alongside a US$600M+ fund-of-funds book, writing US$500K to US$5M pre-seed through Series A+ checks. It invests across the full intelligence stack — model and research layers, AI infrastructure, enterprise and consumer applications, healthcare, education, and robotics and hardware — and has disclosed a portfolio of more than 60 AI-native companies, from foundation-model-adjacent research labs to vertical agents for construction, clinics, law firms and retailers.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Founder-built early-stage VC + fund of funds

thesisHeading: How Llama Ventures invests in AI

thesis.heading: Independent conviction
thesis.body: The firm forms its views before checking the consensus, arguing that insight lives where most investors are not looking. It would rather be non-consensus and right than safely average.

thesis.heading: Human judgment, AI-amplified
thesis.body: AI handles the noise so the partners can focus on founders, markets and timing. Technology sharpens the process, but every conviction remains a human one.

thesis.heading: Depth over breadth
thesis.body: Llama goes deep in the domains it knows and stays honest about what it does not, betting on concentrated expertise and better pattern recognition rather than spreading thin.

thesis.heading: Founder-first partnership
thesis.body: Built by people who have raised capital, shipped products and scaled teams themselves, the firm offers capital, context and candor — hands-on with product, hiring and go-to-market when it matters, invisible when it does not.
